kind: fresh-variant round aimed at json and jsonb documents after T-0272 landed per-leaf masking; three Opus attackers (harmless keys and split values; documents in disguise and odd encodings; cross-stage consistency and the checks that should catch a leak)
orchestrator_note: Every value in every reproduction is invented. The eleven undocumented leaks are fixed by the eight jsonfix tasks filed on 2026-09-25 (personally named document columns mask every leaf; the phone region reaches keys and leaves; the generated-column skip is narrowed to the leaf it reads; one log-shape rule; composites holding a document refuse; json numbers decoded exactly; textsig candidates for fullwidth, dash-separated, mailto:, percent-encoded and base64 spellings; copied leaf keys pinned by the yml), then replayed as round 2 before v0.4.0. The sixteen documented leaks reproduce residuals THREAT_MODEL.md T1's T-0272 amendment and SECURITY.md item 8 name.

attempts_list.attack: A12 (worst): jsonb columns whose own name marks them personal but whose category does not accept jsonb (full_name, home_address, passwords, date_of_birth, national_id) fall back to plain semi_structured, get a leaf map, and every leaf is copied.
attempts_list.fix: The documents promise the opposite. SECURITY.md item 8 says a leaf is still masked for 'every leaf of a column whose own name marks it personal (a `jsonb` `medical_history`)', and T1 says 'every leaf of a document column whose own decision is anything but the classifier's plain semi_structured verdict'. The gap is in pipeline.Decision.LeafMap (internal/pipeline/classify.go:216-221). It returns the map whenever Category == CatSemiStruct && Source == ByClassifier, and the 'jsonb is not an accepted type for X' fallback produces exactly that decision. Fix: when the column's name matched any personal pattern, internal/classify should leave LeafKeys nil or carry a flag LeafMap reads, so every leaf is masked. Better still, mask the leaves under the name's category through leafMasker. Add a regression test for jsonb columns named full_name, address, passwords, date_of_birth, emails, notes and phone. Restate the rule in internal/verify/jsonleaf.go in the same commit.

attempts_list.attack: A13: the same fallback for a free_text-named jsonb (notes) and an email-named jsonb (emails), with a special-category-named jsonb (medical_history) as the control.
attempts_list.fix: Same root cause and fix as A12. SECURITY.md item 8 promises that a column whose own name marks it personal has every leaf masked, but only special_category (accepts: ["*"]) actually reaches that path. Any name hit on a json/jsonb column (free_text, email, phone, address, person_name, credential, person_date, national_id, financial_account and the rest) should null the leaf map.

attempts_list.attack: A11: a national-format phone number used as an object key, in a jsonb column named by_phone.
attempts_list.reproduction:
a11.sql: CREATE TABLE rosters (id integer PRIMARY KEY, by_phone jsonb NOT NULL); INSERT INTO rosters SELECT g, jsonb_build_object('07911 12'||lpad(g::text,4,'0'),'Wren Calloway','+44 7911 13'||lpad(g::text,4,'0'),'Ysolde Brackenridge') FROM generate_series(1,30) g;
Run 1: lazyslice --source .../a11 --target .../a11 --yes --no-config. It exited 0. Reason: 'public.rosters.by_phone: name matches phone; jsonb is not an accepted type for phone; type jsonb is a semi_structured type; no samples'.
psql returned: 1|{"+19075550177": "node profile target", "07911 120001": "Wren Calloway"}. The national phone key survives verbatim and the name under it is copied. The international key and its leaf were masked.
Run 2: the same command plus --phone-region GB. It exited 9: '✗ public.rosters.by_phone is already masked and 30 of its values still validate as phone: --mask cannot change its category, so leave its table out with --skip-table public.rosters' / 'lazyslice: verify.refused.second_net_document_masked ... phone'. The target table was left absent.
attempts_list.fix: There are three problems. (1) The column is named as a phone column, yet its leaves are copied. That is the A12 LeafMap gap, which the documents do not accept. (2) keyCategory (internal/transform/json.go) and strongKeyShape (internal/classify/validators.go) read only textsig.ValidPhone, the international-only check. The second net reads keys under --phone-region, so a run that sets a region fails closed at exit 9, and the only remedy it offers is dropping the table. SECURITY.md item 8 says a key that 'parses as ... a phone number' is masked, which reads as including the run's region. Fix: pass the classification's PhoneRegion to keyCategory and strongKeyShape, using ValidPhoneRegion, so transform masks the key the net would refuse. (3) Without a region, the national-number key survives. That part is within item 8's key-name residual, but it should be closed by the same change.

attempts_list.attack: A1: personal values under keys no name rule matches (attendee, meta.x, data[0].v), plus note, extra and sub.
attempts_list.fix: Accepted residual. THREAT_MODEL.md T1 says a value is copied when 'no name rule on any of its enclosing keys and no value validator recognises is copied — a name under a key like `attendee`', and SECURITY.md item 8 says 'the cost is a personal value no rule and no validator knows, inside a document, which is copied too'. Cheap narrowing: the second net already has a person-name dictionary validator (textsig.Dictionary().NameShape), but applies() in internal/verify/secondnet.go excludes every dict validator from leaves. Add NameShape and ProseName to leafValueCategory on both sides, masking as free_text, so a copied leaf like 'Oswin Harrowgate' or 'Mary Smith' with a dictionary given name and surname is masked. Also correct the 'no samples' reason for decoded-map samples, which is the jsonSignal string-path bug classify/CLAUDE.md already notes. Make the classify/plan output say how many leaf keys will be copied, and name them, so the operator can use the --mask escape hatch knowingly.

attempts_list.attack: A2: key/value-pair documents: [{field, value}], {label: 'full_name', value}, and arrays of {k, v}.
attempts_list.reproduction:
a2.sql: CREATE TABLE form_answers (id integer PRIMARY KEY, answers jsonb NOT NULL, attrs jsonb NOT NULL, pairs jsonb NOT NULL); INSERT INTO form_answers SELECT g, jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('field','email','value','wren.calloway'||g||'@example.test'), jsonb_build_object('field','full_name','value','Wren Calloway'), jsonb_build_object('field','date_of_birth','value','1987-03-1'||(g%10)), jsonb_build_object('field','phone','value','07700 900'||lpad(g::text,3,'0'))), jsonb_build_object('label','full_name','value',(ARRAY['Mary Smith','James Johnson','Wren Calloway'])[1+g%3]), jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('k','surname','v','Calloway'), jsonb_build_object('k','given_name','v','Wren'), jsonb_build_object('k','ni_number','v','QQ 12 34 56 C'), jsonb_build_object('k','city','v','Upper Dunmore')) FROM generate_series(1,30) g;
Commands: lazyslice --source .../a2 --target .../a2 --yes --no-config (exit 0), then the same with --phone-region GB (exit 0). Both runs printed 'the residual scan found nothing (90 value(s) tested)'.
psql (no region) returned: 1|[{"field": "email", "value": "maurice.collins@example.net"}, {"field": "full_name", "value": "Wren Calloway"}, {"field": "date_of_birth", "value": "1987-03-11"}, {"field": "phone", "value": "07700 900001"}]|{"label": "full_name", "value": "James Johnson"}|[{"k": "surname", "v": "Calloway"}, {"k": "given_name", "v": "Wren"}, {"k": "ni_number", "v": "6824 Alder Way"}, {"k": "city", "v": "Upper Dunmore"}]
With GB: select answers->3->>'value', attrs->>'value', answers->2->>'value' returned '07700 900001|James Johnson|1987-03-11'. The phone was still copied in 26 of 30 rows, because libphonenumber rejects the Ofcom drama range 07700 900xxx; rows 3, 10, 19 and 27 were masked by another validator. The email value was masked. Full name, date of birth, surname, given name and city were copied. No refusal.
attempts_list.fix: Accepted residual. SECURITY.md item 8: 'the cost is a personal value no rule and no validator knows, inside a document, which is copied too'. The 07700 900 phone is an artefact of fictional test data; a real GB mobile was masked under --phone-region GB in A4. Fix I would make: an EAV-aware rule. When an object has a string leaf under a descriptor key (field, label, k, key, name, attribute, type) whose value matches a name rule, mask that object's sibling value leaves (value, v, val, answer, data) under the matched category. Transform and verify both see the whole object, so the rule can be restated on both sides the way leafRule is.

attempts_list.attack: A3: one personal value split across leaves: given and family name, a phone as cc plus nsn, an address as l1, l2 and pc.
attempts_list.fix: Accepted residual. T1 says 'a personal value inside a plain `semi_structured` document that no name rule on any of its enclosing keys and no value validator recognises is copied'. Fix I would make: apply the neighbouring-column rule inside one object. When any leaf of an object is masked under person_name, address or phone (by key or by value), mask that object's unnamed sibling string leaves as well, as free_text. Under that rule, masking l1 would carry l2 with it. Also add 'given', 'family', 'first' and 'last' as leaf-key words to the person_name rule, gated on a sibling of the other half, which is the corroboration the bare_name rule already uses.

attempts_list.attack: A4: phones under unnamed keys (national format, split, and as JSON numbers) and card-like numbers stored as JSON numbers.
attempts_list.reproduction:
a4.sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id integer PRIMARY KEY, extra jsonb NOT NULL); INSERT INTO orders SELECT g, jsonb_build_object('a','+44','b','7911 12'||lpad(g::text,4,'0'),'reach','07911 12'||lpad(g::text,4,'0'),'reach_num',('447911'||lpad(g::text,6,'0'))::numeric,'reach_nat_num',('7911'||lpad(g::text,6,'0'))::numeric,'ref_num',4111111111111111,'big_ref',12345678901234567891,'ratio',0.1000000000000000055511151231257827,'ext_id',9007199254740993) FROM generate_series(1,30) g;
Command, no region: lazyslice ... /a4 --yes --no-config. Exit 0, second net silent. psql returned: 1|{"a": "+44", "b": "7911 120001", "ratio": 0.1, "reach": "07911 120001", "ext_id": 206.77, "big_ref": 12345678901234567000, "ref_num": 501.54, "reach_num": 713.69, "reach_nat_num": 7911000001}. Source row 1: {..., "ext_id": 9007199254740993, "big_ref": 12345678901234567891, "ref_num": 4111111111111111, "reach_num": 447911000001, "reach_nat_num": 7911000001}.
With --phone-region GB: exit 0. select extra->>'reach', extra->>'b', extra->'reach_nat_num' returned '+16315550106|+16315550106|392.13'. Every phone form was masked.
Without a region, the national-format phone (string and number) and the split +44/7911 pair were copied, and verify said nothing. The card-number-as-number (ref_num) was masked. Masked integers of a million or more came out fractional (4111111111111111 -> 501.54, 7911000001 -> 392.13), and copied numbers lost precision (big_ref, ratio).
attempts_list.fix: The phone leak without a region is accepted under SECURITY.md item 8: 'the cost is a personal value no rule and no validator knows, inside a document, which is copied too'. The T-0272 amendment ties phone recognition to --phone-region, and the leak closes when the flag is set. Because it silently depends on a flag, the first run should ask for or guess the region when a document holds 10- or 11-digit leading-zero strings, following 'change the default or the question'. The number defects are a separate misbehaviour, reported in A10.

attempts_list.attack: A5: a key whose sampled values are harmless ('n/a', '-', '') while the rows past the 200-row TABLESAMPLE hold names.
attempts_list.fix: Accepted residual. T1: 'a name under a key like `attendee`'. SECURITY.md item 8: 'every key above it appeared in the sampled documents, no name rule names any of them, and no value validator recognises the value'. Fix: as in A1, run the dictionary name validators over copied string leaves on both sides, since the transform sees every row and not only the sample. Also note that the leaf map is outside the fingerprint (ARCHITECTURE §5), so a key whose content changes after the yml is committed never prints 'classification changed'.

attempts_list.attack: A6: the personal leaf sits deeper than any sampled key: a novel key at a new depth, and reused key names at a new depth.
attempts_list.fix: Accepted as written. SECURITY.md item 8 copies a leaf when 'every key above it appeared in the sampled documents'. The map is a set of key names with no positions, so a sampled structure vouches for any structure built from the same names. Fix I would make: key LeafKeys by path shape (the key chain with array indices collapsed, e.g. a.b or opts[].v) rather than by bare name. A leaf is then copied only at a path the samples showed with a scalar there. A scalar path that became an object in an unsampled row (a.b was 'x', now {c: ...}) should also mask. Restate on both sides and extend TestLeafValueCategoryIsPinned.

attempts_list.attack: A7: arrays of documents, and near-miss key names (name, first/last, fn/ln, firstName/lastName, person, owner, user, uid, born), plus a bare array of names.
attempts_list.reproduction:
a7.sql (table renamed from events_cfg to gatherings after the first try; 'events' is log-shaped and collapsed both columns to {}, which is the log-table control holding): CREATE TABLE gatherings (id integer PRIMARY KEY, guests jsonb NOT NULL, who jsonb NOT NULL); INSERT INTO gatherings SELECT g, jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('name','Mary Smith','first','Ottilie','last','Vanderhoek','role','chair'), jsonb_build_object('firstName','Ottilie','lastName','Vanderhoek','fn','Ottilie','ln','Vanderhoek','role','guest'), jsonb_build_object('person','Ottilie Vanderhoek','owner','Ottilie Vanderhoek','user','ottilie.v','uid','8f14e45f-ceea-467a-9575-cd6c1a2f0b3e','born','1990-07-04')), jsonb_build_array('Ottilie Vanderhoek','Mary Smith') FROM generate_series(1,30) g;
Command: lazyslice ... /a7 --yes --no-config. Exit 0.
psql returned: 1|[{"last": "Vanderhoek", "name": "ledger", "role": "chair", "first": "Ottilie"}, {"fn": "Ottilie", "ln": "Vanderhoek", "role": "guest", "lastName": "marker", "firstName": "pointer"}, {"uid": "8f14e45f-...", "born": "1990-07-04", "user": "ottilie.v", "owner": "Ottilie Vanderhoek", "person": "Ottilie Vanderhoek"}]|["scalar item filter", "ledger"]
name, firstName and lastName were masked, and so was the bare array (no key). first, last, fn, ln, person, owner, user, uid and a date of birth under 'born' were copied. `classify --json` emits only 'classify.masked.column' for the column, with no leaf detail.
attempts_list.fix: Accepted residual. SECURITY.md item 8: 'the cost is a personal value no rule and no validator knows, inside a document, which is copied too'. Rule-pack widening I would propose for JSON keys only, where short keys are common: first, last, fn, ln (corroborated by a sibling of the other half), person, owner and born (born alone rather than only born_on), and user (online_id). Also emit the copied leaf keys per column in classify, plan and --json output, so an operator can see 'owner, person, born copied' and apply --mask.

attempts_list.attack: A8/A9: personal values embedded in longer strings under unnamed keys: an email inside a sentence, a mailto: URI, 'ip=...', a card number inside a sentence.
attempts_list.fix: Accepted residual. T1: 'a free-text note under a key no rule names'. SECURITY.md item 6 also covers values 'embedded in a longer string'. But a complete, valid email address sitting inside a leaf is precise enough to act on. Fix: add a substring finder (email, IPv4/IPv6, Luhn-valid 13-19 digit run) to leafValueCategory on both sides and to the net's leaf reading, masking the whole leaf as free_text. Strip a mailto:/tel: scheme before ValidEmail/ValidPhone. None of this needs a dictionary.

attempts_list.attack: A10: number leaves. Copied leaves pass through float64, and masked integers are rebuilt as fractions.
attempts_list.fix: Not a leak but a correctness bug that T-0272 exposed. Before it every leaf was masked, so nobody saw the rounding; now 'copied' means altered. The float64 case in walk (internal/transform/json.go) returns n, the float64, for a copied leaf. Fix: decode with json.Number throughout. Either register a pgx JSON codec that uses Decoder.UseNumber, or fetch json/jsonb as text and use the existing decodeDocument string path, which already uses UseNumber. Then a copied number is byte-for-byte the source spelling. In maskLeafNumber, decide 'fractional' from the value (math.Trunc(f) != f, or no '.' in the 'f' spelling) instead of strings.ContainsAny(in, ".eE") over the 'g' spelling, which writes every integer of a million or more in exponent form. Add a test with a 19-digit id and with 1500000.

attempts_list.attack: A14: document types at the edges: a domain over jsonb, a jsonb[] column, and a text column holding JSON.
attempts_list.reproduction:
a14.sql: CREATE DOMAIN doc_t AS jsonb CHECK (jsonb_typeof(VALUE)='object'); CREATE TABLE intake (id integer PRIMARY KEY, d doc_t NOT NULL, arr jsonb[] NOT NULL, raw_blob text NOT NULL); INSERT INTO intake SELECT g, jsonb_build_object('attendee','Wren Calloway','mail','wren.calloway@example.test'), ARRAY[jsonb_build_object('attendee','Wren Calloway')], jsonb_build_object('attendee','Wren Calloway','kind','x')::text FROM generate_series(1,30) g;
Command: lazyslice ... /a14 --yes --no-config. Exit 0. Reasons: 'arr: ... classified on the element type jsonb; no samples', 'd: type jsonb is a semi_structured type', 'raw_blob: name matches free_text'.
psql returned: 1|{"mail": "lincoln.vargas@example.net", "attendee": "Wren Calloway"}|{"{\"attendee\": \"stack profile\"}"}|scalar routine signal stream profile label
The domain column behaves like jsonb: the email was masked and the attendee copied. jsonb[] had no leaf map and was fully masked, so that control held. The text column was masked whole on its name. My column name tripped the free_text rule, so this did not test JSON-in-text with a neutral name.
attempts_list.fix: The domain behaves like jsonb, so its copied attendee is the accepted residual. T1: 'a name under a key like `attendee`'. jsonb[] held. Follow-up worth running: a text column with a neutral name (e.g. payload_text) holding JSON documents, to see whether the string-path jsonSignal classifies it or it is copied whole. That was not measured here.

attempts_list.attack: A13: a jsonb field inside a composite type. The email sits in the document half of a record column.
attempts_list.reproduction: Schema (a13c.sql): create type wrap as (tag text, doc jsonb); create table widgets (id int primary key, w wrap, w2 wrap); insert into widgets values (1, row('ana.fake@example.org','{"k":"v"}')::wrap, row('a','{"k":"ana.fake@example.org"}')::wrap), (2, row('b','{"k":"v"}')::wrap, row('b','{"k":"z"}')::wrap). Command: PGPASSWORD=pw bin/lazyslice --source 'postgres://postgres:pw@127.0.0.1:48265/s_a13c?sslmode=disable' --target 'postgres://postgres:pw@127.0.0.1:48266/t_a13c?sslmode=disable' --root widgets --secret-file w/secret --config w/lazyslice.yml --yes. Result: exit 12 plan.refused.unwritable on w, where the email is in the text field ('1/2 samples parse as addresses; composite type ... the plan refuses'). w2 was reported as 'composite type: its fields were read and none is personal data'. I dropped w and reran with a13.sql: create domain cfgdoc as jsonb ...; create type wrap as (tag text, doc jsonb); table widgets(id, d cfgdoc, w wrap, g text generated always as (d->>'label') stored); row 1 w = row('a','{"label":"Mary Johnson","m":"ana.fake@example.org"}'). That run exited 0 with no verify refusal. Target check: select * from widgets returned 1|...|(a,"{""m"": ""ana.fake@example.org"", ""label"": ""Mary Johnson""}")|Mary Johnson. The email was copied verbatim. The domain over jsonb (d) was walked correctly: its tel leaf was masked.
attempts_list.fix: The leak is undocumented. THREAT_MODEL T1 says composites fail closed ('a value hit at possible or above is a plan refusal (exit 12)'), but the composite is classified over its record text form. There the JSON is quoted and its quotes are doubled, so ValidEmail never sees a bare address. The second net's composite path has the same blind spot. Fix in internal/classify (and mirror it in verify): parse the record literal into fields, decode any json/jsonb field and run the leaf validators over its leaves. Simpler and safer: refuse at exit 12 any composite that contains a json, jsonb or hstore field, the same as a composite with a hit. Add a regression with an email inside a composite's jsonb field.

attempts_list.attack: A11: a 19-digit Luhn-valid card number stored as a JSON number leaf. pgx decodes jsonb numbers to float64, so the digits past 2^53 are rounded before any validator runs.
attempts_list.reproduction: Schema (a11.sql): create table widgets (id int primary key, b jsonb); insert into widgets values (1, '{"p0":4000123456789012343,"p1":6221260000111122223,"p2":5018000123456789012}'), (2, '{"p0":1,"p1":2,"p2":3}'). All three are invented, Luhn-valid, 19-digit PANs. Command: bin/lazyslice --source .../s_a11 --target .../t_a11 --root widgets --secret-file ... --config ... --yes. Exit 0, no verify refusal. Target check: select b from widgets where id=1 returned {"p0": 4000123456789012500, "p1": 6221260000111122000, "p2": 5018000123456790000}. The first 16 to 17 digits of each PAN (BIN plus most of the account number) reached the target. The rounded 'f' spelling fails Luhn, so leafValueCategory calls the leaf clean and it is copied. A 16-digit card (4111111111111111, which fits in float64) was masked in A1.
attempts_list.fix: This is undocumented. SECURITY item 6 covers the residual scan's canonical equality, not a validator that reads a value transform itself corrupted. Decode json/jsonb without float64: scan the column as raw bytes or text and decode with json.Decoder.UseNumber in internal/transform, and do the same in classify's decodeSampleDocument and in verify's leaf reader. Then validators see the exact digits and the existing json.Number path applies. Add a regression with a 19-digit PAN leaf.

attempts_list.attack: A10 and A1 (misbehaviour): number leaves do not round-trip. Copied big integers are rounded, a jsonb number too large for float64 aborts the run with a misleading message, and every masked integer of 1,000,000 or more becomes a decimal.
attempts_list.reproduction: a10b.sql: create table widgets (id int primary key, b jsonb, j json); row 1 b='{"n1":12345678901234567891,"n2":9007199254740995,"n4":0.1000000000000000055511151231257827,"n5":100000000000000000000000000001}', j='{"n1":12345678901234567891,"n6":1.0}'. Exit 0. Target: {"n1": 12345678901234567000, "n4": 0.1, "n5": 100000000000000000000000000000} and json {"n1":12345678901234567000,"n6":1}. These are 'copied' leaves that no longer equal the source. With "n3":1e400 added (a10.sql), the run exits 1 with 'lazyslice: run.refused.internal: the source catalog could not be read' / 'lazyslice failed for a reason it has no code for'. From A1 (a1.sql, ref: 447700900123, 2079460958, 4111111111111111, ...), the masked integer leaves came back as 778.35, 743.98, 190.59: an integer became a fractional number. In maskLeafNumber, strings.ContainsAny(in, ".eE") tests the 'g' spelling, and Go's shortest 'g' writes any float of 1e6 or more in exponent form ('4.47700900123e+11').
attempts_list.fix: There is no leak, but ARCHITECTURE §4's 'integral stays integral' is broken, and so is the residual-contract claim that a copied leaf means 'the target holds the same value'. Large IDs stored as numbers are silently corrupted. Use the same UseNumber decoding as for A11. Until then, in maskLeafNumber decide integral versus fractional from the value (n == math.Trunc(n)) or from the 'f' spelling, not from the 'g' spelling. Name the out-of-range number as a decode refusal with a code instead of 'source catalog could not be read'.

attempts_list.attack: A7/A7b: odd Unicode encodings in string leaves under neutral keys: fullwidth @ and digits, en-dash or underscore card separators, a trailing-dot domain, a zero-width space, homoglyph keys, duplicate keys and \u escapes.
attempts_list.reproduction: a7b.sql: create table widgets (id int primary key, b jsonb, t text); row 1 b='{"v2":"ana.fake＠example.org","v3":"＋４４ ２０ ７９４６ ０９５８","v5":"4111–1111–1111–1111","v6":"4111/1111/1111/1111","v7":"4111_1111_1111_1111","v8":"ANA.FAKE@EXAMPLE.ORG."}'; rows 2 to 4 hold 'ok'. Command: bin/lazyslice ... --root widgets --yes. Exit 0, no verify refusal. Target: {"v2": "ana.fake＠example.org", "v3": "＋４４ ２０ ７９４６ ０９５８", "v5": "4111–1111–1111–1111", "v6": "1005201857835018", "v7": "4111_1111_1111_1111", "v8": "ANA.FAKE@EXAMPLE.ORG."}. The fullwidth email, the fullwidth international phone, and the en-dash and underscore cards were all copied; only the slash-separated card was masked. In a7.sql, the zero-width email 'ana.fake@exa​mple.org' was masked, and the json column's email key decoded to 'email' and was masked. The homoglyph keys 'phοne' and 'ph​one' holding '020 7946 0958' were copied, but that value is national-format and has no --phone-region, so it would also be copied under a neutral key. The duplicate key in the json column '{"label":"ok","label":"Mary Johnson"}' was silently reduced to the last value and re-sorted: data loss, not a leak. Control a8s.sql shows the same fullwidth and en-dash values copied from a plain text column, so this is a textsig gap, not a JSON-only one.
attempts_list.fix: This is a leak through copied leaves of categories the validators claim to cover. The 2026-09-15 A2 amendment ('Obfuscation is not encryption') promises de-obfuscation, and T1's 'net over recognised shapes only' names unknown shapes, not known shapes in another code point. Fix in internal/textsig Candidates: add an NFKC-normalised candidate (fullwidth ＠ and ＋ and digits to ASCII) and treat Unicode dash punctuation (Pd), '_' and '/' as group separators before collapseGroups. Both nets and leafValueCategory pick this up automatically, and TestLeafValueCategoryIsPinned stays in step.

attempts_list.attack: A4: personal values used as JSON keys: mailto: and prefixed emails, URL-encoded and base64 email keys, a national-format phone key, a person name key, an SSN key and a NINO key, with and without --phone-region GB.
attempts_list.reproduction: a4.sql: create table widgets (id int primary key, seen jsonb); row 1 '{"mailto:mary.j@example.org":"2024-01-02","user:olu.bankole@example.net":"x","MARY.J(at)EXAMPLE.ORG":"y","<tomas.v@example.com>":"z","tomas.v%40example.com":"w","dG9tYXMudkBleGFtcGxlLmNvbQ==":"b64"}'; row 2 '{"020 7946 0958":"called","07700900123":"texted","tel:+442079460958":"x","4111-1111-1111-1111":"card","Mary Johnson":"vip","219-09-9999":"ssn","QQ 12 34 56 C":"nino"}'. The run with --yes exited 9: '✗ public.widgets.seen is already masked and 1 of its values still validate as national_id: --mask cannot change its category, so leave its table out with --skip-table public.widgets'. The target was dropped (relation does not exist). a4b.sql removes the SSN and NINO keys. Without a region it exits 0, and the target keeps the keys 'mailto:mary.j@example.org', 'user:olu.bankole@example.net', 'tomas.v%40example.com', the base64 key, '020 7946 0958', '07700900123' and 'Mary Johnson'. The (at), angle-bracket, tel: and card keys were masked. With --phone-region GB, a4br exits 9: '✗ public.widgets.seen is already masked and 1 of its values still validate as phone: --mask cannot change its category'. transform's keyCategory calls ValidPhone with no region, but the net reads keys under the run's region.
attempts_list.fix: SECURITY item 8 accepts this: 'JSON key names, unless a key itself parses as an email address, a phone number or a credit-card number ... An arbitrary identifier used as a key ... still survives.' A mailto:, prefixed or percent-encoded email does not parse as an address. Still worth fixing: in keyCategory, strip a URI scheme or 'word:' prefix and percent-decode before ValidEmail. It is also a real (fail-closed) misbehaviour that keyCategory and strongKeyShape ignore --phone-region while the net reads keys under it. A document keyed by national numbers can never finish under --phone-region, and the message tells the operator --mask cannot help. Pass the classification's PhoneRegion to keyCategory and strongKeyShape, the same way leafValueCategory gets it. An SSN or NINO-shaped key is likewise unmaskable and only --skip-table-able: add ValidNationalIDStructured to keyCategory so the key is masked instead.

attempts_list.attack: A1/A9: phone numbers as integer leaves and national-format strings under neutral keys, with and without --phone-region.
attempts_list.reproduction: a1.sql: create table widgets (id int primary key, settings jsonb); rows '{"theme":"dark","ref":14155552671}', '{"theme":"dark","ref":2025550143}', '{"theme":"dark","ref":"+14155552671"}', and others. Without a region: exit 0, and the target holds {"ref": 14155552671, ...} and {"ref": 2025550143, ...} copied; the '+1' string was masked to '+15015550112'. With --phone-region US (a1r) everything is masked. a9.sql rows: '{"v1":"020 7946 0958","v2":"07700 900123","v3":2079460958,"v4":7700900123,"v5":"(020) 7946-0958","v6":"0207 946 0958 ext 12","v7":"tel 020 7946 0958"}'. With no flag, exit 0 and all copied verbatim. With --phone-region GB, exit 0 and v1, v3, v5, v6 and v7 masked (to US-format '+1...' fakes). v2 and v4, in Ofcom's 07700 900xxx drama range, were copied because libphonenumber treats them as invalid, and the net agrees.
attempts_list.fix: THREAT_MODEL T1 (T-0221) accepts this: a national-format number 'scored zero on both nets' without a region, and '--phone-region REGION ... is the fix'. The T-0272 amendment also states that the value half reads the phone 'under the run's --phone-region'. Improvements: offer a number leaf of 11 to 15 digits to ValidPhone as '+'+digits, since an E.164 number stored without its plus is common in JSON. Carry the configured region into the phone masker so a GB leaf is not replaced by a +1 number.

attempts_list.attack: A3/A2b/A5b/A6: a personal value under a key no rule names, or under a key that also holds harmless values: a key case and spacing sweep, names under attendee/guest/contact/label, a date of birth under bday, a subject id under sub, a top-level array of objects, JSON in varchar and json columns, and a document with more than 4,096 keys.
attempts_list.reproduction: a3.sql: table widgets(id, profile jsonb), one row with the keys E-Mail, e mail, eMail, EMAIL, Full Name, fullName, full-name, FULLNAME, firstName, Surname, DOB, Date Of Birth, dateOfBirth, bday, birth-date, Phone No., tel, mobileNumber, handy, SSN, socialSecurityNumber, ss_no, nino, zip, postCode, addr1, lat, lng, nickname, gender, religion, ethnicity, salary, username, attendee, guest, contact, sub. Exit 0. Every case and spacing variant of email, name, DOB, phone, SSN and address was masked. Copied: "bday": "1984-03-12", "attendee"/"guest"/"contact": "Mary Johnson", "salary": 85000, "sub": "a3f1c2d4e5b6978812345678abcdef01". a5b.sql, top-level array '[{"n":1,"label":"Mary Johnson"},"plain",{"label":"ok"}]': the label was copied and the bare element masked. a2b.sql, varchar meta '{"k":"v","who":"Marta Quellberg"}' and json blob '{"attendee":"Oskar Brindlemoor"}': both copied, exit 0. a6.sql has 4,100 keys k00000..k04099 plus aaa_label and zzz_label: 'aaa_label' (inside the sorted 4,096) kept 'Mary Johnson'; 'zzz_label' past the limit was masked ('stack limit'), and row 2's zzz_label masked ('index series'). A key seen in the samples with harmless values ('label':'ok') and a name in another row copies the name, while an email in the same slot is masked per row by the validator.
attempts_list.fix: THREAT_MODEL T1's T-0272 amendment accepts this: 'a personal value inside a plain semi_structured document that no name rule on any of its enclosing keys and no value validator recognises is copied — a name under a key like `attendee`, an identity provider's subject id under `sub`, a free-text note under a key no rule names.' SECURITY item 8 says the same. Cheap recall wins: add the name dictionary's given-plus-surname test (Dict.LooksLikeName) to leafValueCategory. 'Mary Johnson' is two Census-top names that the scalar path would count and the leaf path ignores. Add 'bday', 'birthday', 'dob' variants, and 'salary' and 'contact', to the rule pack. The 4,096-key limit and the key-variant normalisation held.

attempts_list.attack: A12: very long string leaves and prose with an embedded email, phone or card under a neutral key.
attempts_list.reproduction: a12.sql: widgets(id, b jsonb). Row 1: label='Please call Ana at ana.fake@example.org tomorrow'; label2 = 108 KB of lorem plus ' contact ana.fake@example.org ' plus lorem; label3='Ring me on +44 20 7946 0958 after six'; label4 = lorem plus ' card 4111 1111 1111 1111 ' plus lorem; label5 = 600 x's followed directly by 'ana.fake@example.org'. Exit 0. Target check: b->>'label' returned the prose with the email verbatim, and ~ 'ana.fake@example.org' was true for label2 and label5 and ~ '4111 1111' was true for label4. label3 was masked, as address. Control a12s.sql, the same prose in a scalar text column 'label', was also copied at exit 0 ('nothing recognised in 4 samples').
attempts_list.fix: T1 accepts this: 'They are a net over recognised shapes only' and 'a free-text note under a key no rule names'. The leaf path behaves the same as the scalar path. This is still the cheapest large win: in leafValueCategory and in the net, add an embedded-token scan (split on whitespace and punctuation, run ValidEmail, ValidPhone and ValidLuhn over each token, capped at N tokens) for string leaves longer than one token. For a leaf over maxCandidateLen, mask it as free_text rather than copy it, because a long unkeyed prose leaf is free text by shape.

attempts_list.attack: A8: base64, URL-encoded and mailto: leaves.
attempts_list.reproduction: a8.sql: widgets(id, b jsonb). Row 1: v1 = base64('ana.fake@example.org'), v2 = 'ana.fake%40example.org', v3 = 'mailto:ana.fake@example.org', v4 = base64 of '{"name":"Mary Johnson","phone":"+442079460958"}', v5 = '%2B442079460958', v6 = 'ana.fake+tag@example.org', v7 = 'Mary Johnson <mary.j@example.org>', v8 = 'name=Mary%20Johnson&tel=%2B442079460958', v9 = unpadded base64 of the email. Row 2 holds 'ok' everywhere. Exit 0. Target: v1, v2, v4, v8 and v9 became '$lazyslice$invalid' (credential entropy masker); v6 and v7 became fake emails. Copied: "v3": "mailto:ana.fake@example.org" and "v5": "%2B442079460958". Control a8s.sql shows 'mailto:ana.fake@example.org' also copied from a plain text column.
attempts_list.fix: Base64 held only by accident of entropy: a longer base64 blob of low-entropy text could fall under LooksSecret's threshold. mailto: and percent-encoded values are known categories in a trivially reversible spelling; T1's accepted residual names shapes outside the list, not these. Fix in textsig Candidates: add a candidate with a leading 'mailto:'/'tel:'/'sms:' scheme stripped, and a percent-decoded candidate when the value contains %XX. Optionally add a base64-decoded candidate when the decode is printable UTF-8.

attempts_list.attack: A5/A14: disguised containers: jsonb[], json[], hstore, top-level scalars, and a jsonb string scalar that holds double-encoded JSON (the Rails serialized-column shape).
attempts_list.reproduction: a5.sql: widgets(id, arr jsonb, docs jsonb[], hs hstore, scal jsonb, jarr json[]). Row 1: docs=array['{"note":"Mary Johnson","k":"v"}'::jsonb], hs='note=>"Mary Johnson", email=>"ana.fake@example.org"', scal='"Mary Johnson"', jarr=array['{"note":"Mary Johnson"}'::json]. Exit 0. docs and jarr had every leaf masked ('classified on the element type jsonb; no samples'); hs became ''; scal became {} (a jsonb string became an object); scal 42 became 208156. a14.sql: b = to_jsonb('{"m":"ana.fake@example.org","label":"ok"}'::text), a jsonb string. Target: {"m": "fernando.haynes@example.org", "label": "ok"} with jsonb_typeof 'object', not 'string'. The string 'plain words' became {}.
attempts_list.fix: No leak: arrays of documents, hstore and scalars all masked or collapsed. It is a fidelity bug that breaks applications. decodeDocument treats every Go string as a text carrier to parse, but for a json/jsonb column pgx already decoded the value, so a Go string there is a JSON string scalar. Decide on the column's type family and not the Go kind: for json/jsonb, walk a string as a string leaf (chain empty, so it is masked as free_text), and parse only for a domain, hstore or unregistered carrier. Mirror the change in classify's decodeSampleDocument so key collection agrees.

attempts_list.attack: A15/A2: escape hatches and fail-closed paths: a JSON document in a text column with an email leaf, and --mask on a document column.
attempts_list.reproduction: a2.sql: widgets(id, prefs text, meta varchar(500), blob json). prefs row 1 = '{"theme":"dark","owner":"ines.fakeperson@example.org"}', row 2 = '{"theme":"light","owner":"+442079460958"}'. Exit 9: '✗ public.widgets.prefs is not masked and 1 of its values validate as email: mask it with --mask public.widgets.prefs=email, or leave its table out with --skip-table public.widgets'. The target was dropped ('the last run left personal data in it'; relation widgets does not exist afterwards). a15.sql (the a3 document) with --mask public.widgets.profile=semi_structured: exit 0, and attendee, bday, sub, salary and contact all became filler ('field format', 'unit panel', ..., 511465).
attempts_list.fix: Both held. The second net reads JSON inside a text column and refuses at exit 9 with the target dropped, and --mask masks every leaf as SECURITY item 8 promises. One small suggestion: for a text column whose values parse as JSON objects, the refusal could suggest --mask TABLE.COL=semi_structured, which keeps the structure, instead of =email, which replaces the whole document with one fake address.

attempts_list.attack: Generated column that assembles an email, a phone number and a card number from copied leaves of a masked jsonb (the auth.identities shape). The second-net skip applies to the whole generated column for every leaf-masker category, not just to the leaf it reads.
attempts_list.reproduction:
Scratch: /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-json-2/a2b.sql. Disposable postgres:16 source and target on random ports (run.sh).
CREATE TABLE identities (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, identity_data jsonb NOT NULL,
  email text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (lower(identity_data ->> 'email')) STORED,
  joined text GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((identity_data ->> 'u') || '@' || (identity_data ->> 'h')) STORED,
  dial text GENERATED ALWAYS AS ('+' || (identity_data ->> 'cc') || (identity_data ->> 'nsn')) STORED,
  dial_n text GENERATED ALWAYS AS ('+' || (identity_data ->> 'n')) STORED,
  pan text GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((identity_data ->> 'bin') || (identity_data ->> 'tail')) STORED);
INSERT INTO identities (id, identity_data) SELECT g, jsonb_build_object('email','quillon.varda'||g||'@fictionmail.example','u','quillon.varda'||g,'h','fictionmail.example','cc','44','nsn','2079460'||lpad(g::text,3,'0'),'n',('442079460'||lpad(g::text,3,'0'))::bigint,'bin','411111','tail','1111111111') FROM generate_series(1,30) g;
Command: bin/lazyslice --source $SRC --target $TGT --root identities --yes --secret-file ../secret.key --no-config (no --phone-region).
The classifier saw the source's generated columns: 'public.identities.joined: 30/30 samples parse as addresses', 'dial: 30/30 samples valid E.164', 'pan: 30/30 samples pass the Luhn check'. It still copied the leaves u, h, cc, nsn, bin and tail, because no rule or validator recognises any of them alone.
Exit 0: 'verify: ... the residual scan found nothing (30 value(s) tested), the second net scanned 7 column(s)'.
Target (psql `select id,email,joined,dial,pan from identities`): '1 | celia.camacho@example.com | quillon.varda1@fictionmail.example | +442079460001 | 4111111111111111'. That is the real email, the real E.164 phone and a Luhn-valid PAN for all 30 rows.
Control, same run: I added scalar columns u and h and `joined2 GENERATED AS (u||'@'||h)`, then ran with --unmask 'identities.u=red-team control'. Exit 9: 'public.identities.joined2 is not masked and 30 of its values validate as email'. So the netColumn skip (secondnet.go, `mode.derivedFromMaskedLeaves && leafMaskerEmits(val.category)`) is the only thing that lets `joined` through.
The Supabase column itself (`email = lower(identity_data->>'email')`) held: it holds the masker's fake.
attempts_list.fix: Narrow the skip from the column to the leaf. In netColumn, for a derivedFromMaskedLeaves column, skip a hit only when the generated value equals (after lower/btrim) a string leaf of the same row's document that leafRule says a category masker replaced (replacedByCategoryMasker). Every other hit counts as usual, so the net sees a value built from copied leaves. At plan time, internal/classify should raise the keys a generated column's expression reads (exprIdentifiers plus the ->>/-> literals) to that column's own category whenever the source samples of the generated column validate (it already computes '30/30 samples parse as addresses'), so the leaves are masked in the first place. The residual is named only in jsonleaf.go's comment on generatedFromMaskedLeaves ('an expression that assembles a personal value out of copied leaves'), not in THREAT_MODEL T1 or SECURITY item 8. Separately, the refusal hint '--mask public.identities.joined2=email' names a generated column, which ARCHITECTURE's --mask row says is exit 2.

attempts_list.attack: The log-shape rule in the classifier and the one in transform disagree. A CamelCase log table ("AuditLog", which is Prisma's default) and an *_activity table are reported as 'replaced whole', but transform walks them leaf by leaf and copies leaves that have no signal.
attempts_list.fix: Keep a single log-shape rule. Put a LogShaped flag on pipeline.Decision, set it in internal/classify from the rule pack's regex over the normalised table name (inside Classification.Fingerprint), and have transform's maskDocument and verify read that flag instead of logTableWords. Add a test that asserts every table the reasons line calls 'replaced whole' comes out as {}. Before T-0272 the mismatch was harmless because every walked leaf was masked. Now the plan tells the operator a document is replaced whole while leaves without a signal are copied. T1 says only that 'a log-shaped table and an hstore still collapse to {}', which is exactly what fails here.

attempts_list.attack: National-format phone number under a leaf key the name rules miss, with no --phone-region. The same value in a scalar column of the same name is masked on a guessed-region hit, but the leaf is copied.
attempts_list.reproduction:
Scratch: a12.sql.
CREATE TABLE members (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, "whatsApp" text, ...14 other camelCase personal columns..., doc jsonb NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO members SELECT g, ..., '020 7946 6'||lpad(g::text,3,'0'), ..., jsonb_build_object('whatsApp','020 7946 6'||lpad(g::text,3,'0'), 'mobileNumber', ..., 'dateOfBirth','14/03/1987', 'givenName','Quillon', ...) FROM generate_series(1,25) g;
Command: lazyslice --source $SRC --target $TGT --root members --yes --secret-file ../secret.key --no-config (no --phone-region).
The scalar was masked: 'public.members.whatsApp: 25/25 samples parse as phone numbers under a guessed region; ... masked on a guessed-region hit corroborated by name or a personal neighbour'.
Exit 0.
Target `select jsonb_pretty(doc) from members where id=1` shows "whatsApp": "020 7946 6001", the source value, in all 25 rows. Every other camelCase leaf key (mobileNumber, homePhone, WorkTel, cellNo, phoneNr, contactNumber, faxNumber, givenName, familyName, dateOfBirth, streetAddress, zipCode, taxId, ssnLast4) was masked, so key-name parity holds everywhere except here.
attempts_list.fix: Give the per-key map a value half. When collectJSONKeys finds that one key's string leaves across the samples parse as phone numbers under the guessed-region list, at the same ratio and corroboration the scalar path uses (a personal key or neighbour in the same document or table), jsonKeyCategories should give that key CatPhone. transform then masks every leaf under it, and the net's skip remains sound because the leaf is category-masked. Alternatively, when a document column sits in a table that already holds a guessed-region phone decision, pass that region to leafPolicy. The T1 amendment names the region gap only as the pre-review-round bug fixed 'with the flag'. It does not accept a national number copied without the flag when the scalar path masks it.

attempts_list.attack: Person names under leaf keys that are common in real documents (author, recipient, attendee, contact_person, guest, emergency). The bare word `name` was tested too.
attempts_list.reproduction:
Scratch: a4.sql. accounts.prefs = jsonb_build_object('name','Quillon Varda<X>','author','Quillon Vardanek','recipient','Ysolde Pembrook','attendee','Ysolde Pembrook','contact_person','Ysolde Pembrook','pronouns','she/her','salary',85000+g,'vat','GB123456789','firstName','Quillon','surname','Vardanek','dob',...,'passport_no',...,'theme','dark',...) for 25 rows. A later update added 'guest','Ysolde Pembrook' and 'emergency','Ysolde Pembrook, sister'.
Command: lazyslice --source $SRC --target $TGT --root accounts --yes --secret-file ../secret.key --config ./lazyslice.yml. Exit 0, and verify found nothing.
Target `select jsonb_pretty(prefs) from accounts where id=1` has these copied verbatim: "author": "Quillon Vardanek", "recipient": "Ysolde Pembrook", "attendee": "Ysolde Pembrook", "contact_person": "Ysolde Pembrook", "pronouns": "she/her", "salary": 85001, "vat": "GB123456789", and later "guest"/"emergency".
These were masked: name, firstName, surname, dob, birthday, born_on, gender, ethnicity, passport_no, username, nickname, postcode, city, plate, note.
attempts_list.fix: THREAT_MODEL T1's T-0272 amendment accepts this: 'a personal value inside a plain `semi_structured` document that no name rule on any of its enclosing keys and no value validator recognises is copied — a name under a key like `attendee`'. To shrink it, add author, recipient, attendee, guest, contact_person, emergency(_contact), pronouns and salary to rules.yml's person_name, special and financial patterns (they help scalar columns too). Also consider a leaf-level person_name dictionary check at a given-name-plus-surname shape when a sibling key in the same object is already personal. The operator's escape hatch (--mask TABLE.COL=semi_structured) works: see the escape-hatch attempt.

attempts_list.attack: Re-run from a committed lazyslice.yml after new keys appear in the source documents. The leaf map is not in the fingerprint, so the drift and --strict-schema checks never see that more leaves are now copied.
attempts_list.reproduction:
Scratch: a4. Run 1 wrote ./lazyslice.yml (its accounts.prefs entry holds only category/confidence/reason/masker/type, with no key list). Then on the source:
UPDATE accounts SET prefs = prefs || jsonb_build_object('guest','Ysolde Pembrook','emergency','Ysolde Pembrook, sister');
Command: lazyslice --source $SRC --target $TGT --root accounts --yes --secret-file ../secret.key --config ./lazyslice.yml --strict-schema
Output: '12 decisions from ./lazyslice.yml, 0 drift, 0 changed', then exit 0.
Target `select prefs->>'guest', prefs->>'emergency' from accounts where id=1` gives 'Ysolde Pembrook|Ysolde Pembrook, sister'.
`diff run1.yml lazyslice.yml` shows only the header timestamp and snapshot_id. A reviewer who approved the committed yml never sees the new copied keys.
Same-data re-runs held: run 2 from the unchanged yml produced the same leaf decisions (author copied, name masked, theme copied).
attempts_list.fix: Record the sorted set of copied leaf keys on each document column's yml entry, under a `leaf_keys:` or `copied_keys:` list, or at least a hash of it. On a re-run, a key the samples show that the yml does not list counts as drift. Mask it (as a key never seen is masked today) until the yml is re-approved, and under --strict-schema exit 10. ARCHITECTURE §5 'Determinism scope' mentions that the map is outside the fingerprint. Neither THREAT_MODEL T1 nor SECURITY item 8 says that a committed yml does not pin which leaves are copied.

attempts_list.attack: The same email in a scalar column and in a leaf: are the fakes consistent, and does an FK through a generated column over the leaf hold?
attempts_list.reproduction:
Part A (scratch a1.sql):
users(id pk, email varchar(120) NOT NULL UNIQUE, profile jsonb {'email': same address, 'theme','dark','lang','en'})
invites(invitee_email varchar(120), same addresses, no FK)
user_settings(settings jsonb {'notify_to': address,'digest':'weekly'})
Using zorblat.quenn<n>@fictionmail.test. After I dropped the email FK, exit 0.
Target: users.email for id 1 = 'colin.mclaughlin.aqpn5vp5al6nf@example.com', while profile->>'email' and settings->>'notify_to' = 'colin.mclaughlin@example.com'. `count(*) filter (where u.email=u.profile->>'email')` = 0 of 40.
The leaf and the non-unique scalar do agree: invites.invitee_email for the address of users.id 2 is 'jerome.brewer@example.net', which equals users 2's leaf. The UNIQUE scalar gets the injective generator and the leaf gets the small-domain one, so equality between a unique column and a leaf is lost.
Part B (scratch a7.sql):
CREATE TABLE users (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, email text NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE orders (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, user_id bigint REFERENCES users(id), meta jsonb NOT NULL, buyer_email text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (meta ->> 'buyer_email') STORED REFERENCES users(email));
Command: lazyslice ... --root users --yes --secret-file ../secret.key --no-config.
Exit 8: 'the foreign key orders_buyer_email_fkey on public.orders does not validate: the slice is missing rows it references' (SQLSTATE 23503).
Target: buyer_email 'celia.camacho@example.com' vs users.email 'celia.camacho.quf3fcccqs3dg@example.com'.
The target is left loaded and the FK is left NOT VALID.
Nothing leaked.
attempts_list.fix: No leak. Two misbehaviours. (1) Plan equality groups ignore an FK whose child is a generated column over a document leaf. Fold such a column into the group and mask the leaf the expression reads with the group's masker, or refuse at plan (exit 12) naming the leaf, instead of failing at load with a message that blames missing rows. (2) Use the unique column's injective email generator for a leaf too, or for every email in the run, so that a leaf that copies users.email keeps equality. A leaf has no uniqueness constraint, and a wider domain only lowers the collision rate the leafMasker comment worries about.

attempts_list.attack: A plain FK between two email columns, one UNIQUE (the equality-group side of the same inconsistency).
attempts_list.reproduction:
Scratch: a1.sql with its original FK: invites.invitee_email varchar(120) REFERENCES users(email), where users.email is varchar(120) NOT NULL UNIQUE.
Command: lazyslice --source $SRC --target $TGT --root users --yes --secret-file ../secret.key.
Exit 12, plan.refused.equality_group: 'email — the widest masker email has for them — emits 2874000 distinct value(s) in public.invites.invitee_email but 9223372036854775807 in public.users.email ... --unmask every column of the group — public.invites.invitee_email, public.users.email, each with its own =REASON'.
Nothing was written.
attempts_list.fix: No leak, since the run refused. But the only remedy the refusal offers is to unmask both ends, which copies every real address into the target. That turns an FK on an email column, a common schema shape, into pressure to disable masking. Choose the injective generator for every member of a group when any member is unique (the child side never needs the smaller domain), and remove the unmask advice from this hint.

attempts_list.attack: A log-shaped table that is collapsed to {} and has real FK children, one of them referencing a UNIQUE generated column over the collapsed document (the webhook_events.external_id pattern).
attempts_list.fix: No leak. Misbehaviour: the plan should detect that a generated column over a collapsed or masked document is a referenced key. It should then refuse at plan (exit 12), naming the column and offering --skip-table or a --mask on the child, or put the child into an equality group with the parent's recomputed value. It should not mask the child with a credential fixed value and fail FK validation at exit 8. Also, the exit-8 message blames missing rows when the real cause is a masking mismatch. And a failed run leaves loaded rows and NOT VALID constraints in the target; that deserves a line in the failure output.

attempts_list.attack: Operator escape hatch: --mask TABLE.COL=semi_structured, the committed mask: block it writes, and --mask with other categories on a document column.
attempts_list.reproduction:
Scratch: a4. Command: lazyslice --source $SRC --target $TGT --root accounts --yes --secret-file ../secret.key --config ./lazyslice.yml --mask accounts.prefs=semi_structured.
Reason line: 'raised by lazyslice.yml for this column'; output: '0 drift, 1 changed'; exit 0.
Target prefs for id 1: every string leaf is filler ('author': 'policy limit', 'recipient': 'pattern packet', 'theme': 'thread', 'guest': 'pattern packet') and every number leaf is re-derived.
The yml gained `mask: {category: semi_structured, by: flag}`. A re-run from that yml without the flag kept it ('policy limit|thread|pattern packet').
With --mask accounts.prefs, =email or =person_name the run exits 2: 'it is already masked as semi_structured, and --mask never changes a column's masker; drop the flag, or name --mask public.accounts.prefs=semi_structured'.

attempts_list.attack: The second net against personal values used as object keys (IP, URL, IBAN) and against a national phone leaf under --phone-region, including region persistence and override on a re-run.
attempts_list.reproduction:
Scratch: a6.sql.
CREATE TABLE devices (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, label text, meta jsonb NOT NULL);
meta = {'memo':'020 7946 0<nnn>','pager':20794600000+g,'seen_from':{'10.20.30.<g>':{'state':'up'}},'links':{'https://quillon.example/u/qv<g>':true},'accounts':{'GB82WEST12345698765432':1}}

(a) With the IP key: exit 9, 'public.devices.meta is already masked and 20 of its values still validate as network_id: ... --skip-table public.devices'. The target table was dropped.
(b) With the IP key removed (URL key present): exit 9, 'validate as online_id'.
(c) With the URL key removed: exit 0, and the target holds {"memo": "policy margin", "pager": 20794600001, "accounts": {"GB82WEST12345698765432": 1}}. The IBAN key survived verbatim, because the net's IBAN entry is not strong and the key is 1 hit among 3+ strings per document. The number leaf pager is copied, and the net never reads number leaves.
(d) The memo leaf was masked under GB. yml recorded 'phone_region: GB'. A re-run from the yml with no flag and one with --phone-region US both kept memo masked ('policy margin').
attempts_list.fix: The IBAN key leak is SECURITY item 8: 'An arbitrary identifier used as a key — a UUID, a slug, a customer number — is not named by any of the three and still survives.' To shrink it, have transform's keyCategory mask any key that leafValueCategory recognises (IBAN, IP, URL, national id), not only email, phone and Luhn. That also turns the IP and URL cases, which today are exit 9 with --skip-table as the only way out, into correct runs. Have the net read number leaves through their plain decimal spelling, the way transform's rule does. The region handling held.

attempts_list.attack: Number-leaf fidelity: large integers in copied leaves and in masked leaves.
attempts_list.reproduction:
Scratch: a4 and a2b. Leaf 'tweet_id': 1234567890123456789 (copied, no signal). Target prefs->>'tweet_id' = '1234567890123456800': pgx decodes jsonb into float64, so a copied leaf is silently rounded.
A masked integer leaf ≥ 1e6 comes back fractional. a2b's 'n': 442079460001 became 997.89. a4's 'big': 9007199254740993 became 436.29. Under --mask, 'tweet_id' became 75.77.
The cause is in transform walk's float64 arm: `in := strconv.FormatFloat(n, 'g', -1, 64)` writes '4.42079460001e+11', and maskLeafNumber treats any 'e' as fractional. That breaks the §4 'integral stays integral' promise and the application's types.
No personal value was involved in the copy. Exit 0 every time.
attempts_list.fix: No leak. It is a correctness bug in json.go. Have pgx hand json/jsonb back as text (or []byte) and decode it with UseNumber, which the string path already does, so copied leaves are exact. Decide integrality from the json.Number spelling, or from float64 == math.Trunc, rather than from a 'g' rendering. Add a regression test for a 19-digit id leaf copied exactly and for a 12-digit integer leaf masked to an integer.

attempts_list.attack: Residual scan on leaf fakes: a source leaf that already equals another row's fake at the same path.
attempts_list.reproduction:
Scratch: a9.sql.
CREATE TABLE contacts (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, card jsonb NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (1,'{"email":"zorblat.quenn1@fictionmail.test","kind":"primary"}'),(2,'{"email":"colin.mclaughlin@example.com","kind":"primary"}') plus 10 fillers.
I chose row 2's value from a1, where row 1's address masked to colin.mclaughlin@example.com under the same key.
Command: lazyslice ... --root contacts --yes --secret-file ../secret.key --no-config.
Exit 9: 'residual hits in public.contacts.card could not be confirmed: a masked JSON leaf cannot be confirmed by an equality probe on the column'.
The scalar control (contacts2.email with the same two values) also exits 9, with 'the source still holds this value in this column'.
attempts_list.fix: Held: it fails closed and nothing leaks. It is a false refusal, reachable whenever the source already holds fixture-like firstname.lastname@example.* addresses from the fake vocabulary. Use the injective generator for leaf emails, or exclude the fake-vocabulary domain (example.com/.net/.org) from masker output collisions by re-drawing. The scalar message 'the source still holds this value' is misleading on a collision and should say that the fake coincided with another row's source value.
